input.quote: 13.4.1 Without the prior written consent of the other Party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, neither Party shall sell, transfer, assign, delegate, pledge, or otherwise dispose of, whether voluntarily, involuntarily, by operation of law or otherwise, this Agreement or any of its rights or duties hereunder; provided that either Party may make such an assignment without the other Party's consent to its Affiliate or to a successor, whether in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or any other transaction, of the business to which this Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 13.4.1 gives AbbVie (our party) an express consent-free carve-out to assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, sale of stock or sale of assets, and any other assignment requires consent that may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. The restriction is mutual, so Harpoon is subject to the same consent standard. Change of control is addressed only in Section 13.2 ("Change in Control of Harpoon"), which imposes a notice obligation on Harpoon and, together with Sections 2 (p0273) and 5 (p0369), gives AbbVie rights where Harpoon is acquired by a Competitor; nothing in the Agreement gives Harpoon a termination or re-pricing right on an AbbVie change of control. This meets the preferred position on the material terms. Two minor sub-elements short of the ideal are noted but not flagged: the clause does not expressly bar Harpoon from assigning to an AbbVie competitor, and the mutual (rather than one-way) consent requirement is a symmetrical bargain we accept in this collaboration structure.
